text: When you build a REST API, good design makes it easier for others to use. Start by giving your endpoints clear, meaningful names, such as /users or /orders. Use the correct HTTP methods and return proper status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Always write clear documentation so developers understand how each endpoint works. It is also important to use versioning, for example /v1/users, so that future changes do not break existing applications. Following these simple practices helps you create APIs that are reliable, consistent, and easy to maintain over time.
